plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay only that second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated interaction to exploit, the safest and most profit-maximizing action is to bid exactly my private value of $20.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value risks paying more than the item is worth, while bidding below risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to adjust for, I'll bid exactly my private value of $45 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win, and bidding truthfully ensures you win whenever it's profitable to do so. With my value at $44, I will bid exactly $44 to guarantee I never overpay or miss profitable wins.
